steps.prompt: A $\$60$ jacket is $25\%$ off, then a further $10\%$ off the sale price. Is that the same as $35\%$ off? Why or why not?

cards.title: Percent as a multiplier
cards.body: $p\%$ of a number is $\frac{p}{100}$ times it. A $p\%$ increase multiplies by $1 + \frac{p}{100}$ and a $p\%$ decrease by $1 - \frac{p}{100}$. Percent change $= \frac{\text{new} - \text{old}}{\text{old}} \times 100\%$: always divide by the original.

cards.title: Worked example: two discounts
cards.problem: A $\$60$ jacket is $25\%$ off, then a further $10\%$ off the sale price. What is the final price, and what single discount is that?

try.prompt: What is the final price, in dollars?

steps.text: The price fell by $60 - 40.5 = 19.5$ dollars out of $60$.

try.prompt: What single percent discount is that?

steps.text: So it is $32.5\%$ off, not $35\%$: the $10\%$ is taken from a smaller price.

cards.title: Worked example: converting units
cards.problem: A car uses $6$ litres of fuel per $100$ km. How many litres does it need for a $350$ km trip?

steps.text: Write the rate as a fraction: $\frac{6 \text{ litres}}{100 \text{ km}}$.
Multiply by the distance so the km cancel: $350 \text{ km} \times \frac{6 \text{ litres}}{100 \text{ km}}$.

cards.title: Ratios and proportions
cards.body: A ratio $a : b$ splits a total into $a + b$ equal parts. In a proportion $\frac{a}{b} = \frac{c}{d}$, cross-multiply: $ad = bc$. Check that the units match on both sides.

prompts: Why is $25\%$ off and then $10\%$ off not the same as $35\%$ off?
